title: Tax registration, tax election and tax determination are different things
summary: A TaxRegistration records the statutory relationship with a tax authority. An effective-dated TaxElection freezes the exact ruleset identity, rounding algorithm, calculation granularity and return scheme. A TaxDetermination applies the elected jurisdiction policy to exact supply evidence. None of those is inferred from domicile.
invariants: TaxRegistration belongs to a legal entity independently of incorporation country or establishment.
One foreign legal entity may hold a GB VAT registration without a fictional UK company or UK establishment.
Changing an elected calculation/rounding method prospectively does not require inventing a new tax registration number.
Tax policy dispatch is by exact rulesetIdentity, not by country name or a mutable current-rules label.
The tax policy decides taxability, classification, rate/formula and legal rounding interpretation; Accounting Core supplies generic mechanics and validates evidence binding.
Tax determination does not choose GL accounts; it produces an evidence-bound result that enters the ordinary legal-entity accounting-policy path.
Already-accounted tax requests are replay-checked before newer tax/accounting policies can reinterpret them.

provenance.claim: TaxRegistration is distinct from effective-dated TaxElection and from legal-entity domicile/establishment.
Generic tax determination dispatches exact jurisdiction ruleset identity and produces evidence-bound results without embedding tax law in the ledger.
